blocks.1: Church service at the Gulating Millennium Site the day after the opening on 27 August 2005.
blocks.2: Our history shows that the old Gulating was the gathering place for the people of a large area, from Sunnmøre in the north to the Agder counties in the south. Valdres, Hallingdal and Setesdal also belonged to it, as did the islands in the North Sea until they got their own law district.
blocks.3: Here the farmers had their laws and rules adopted, and here breaches of the law were judged. They also came here to meet kinsmen and friends, hear the news, trade and simply relax. In the oldest times it was perhaps the religious gatherings at the great sacrificial festivals that drew the most people. Religious and legal ceremonies were performed here before large crowds.
blocks.4: It is no wonder that the idea of a memorial to these important gatherings, which meant so much to a whole people, began to take shape among the people early on. This was a matter not only for our municipality but of national, and some even claimed international, scope and interest. The cause has had many champions over the years, both those we know of today and many who are forgotten.
blocks.5: One of the first we read of here who was concerned with the Gulating and put it “on the map”, as we say today, was Dean Niels Griis Alstrup Dahl. Among all his interests, his interest in our history was great. He and the cantor Furnæs travelled together around the parish and wrote down the legends and traditions found among the people. He believed that both old Gaulom, with its great heathen temple and well-known place of sacrifice, and the Gulating were here. In “Budstikken” in 1824, Dahl, the district judge Blom and Lieutenant Colonel Holck exchanged articles about the Gulating. After that there seem to have been no voices doubting that the assembly stood in Gulen.
blocks.6: But as to the site within the municipality, a great many people have had, and voiced, opinions. When the idea of a Gulating memorial came up, the debate about “the right assembly site” broke out in earnest. From the material I have read, it was Otto J. Midtun (Henriksbø) who first “publicly” raised the question of raising a Gulating memorial. In an article dated 19 November 1910, printed in “Sogns Tidende” on 13 January 1911, he writes that at “the youth rally in Eivindvik this summer” he had stressed “how necessary it would be to raise a memorial stone at the old Gulating site.” At this rally 33.37 kroner had been collected; later 1 krone came in, making 34.37 kroner in all. The idea was that when enough money had come in, a committee would be elected to be responsible for raising the memorial.
blocks.7: In the article he urges youth societies to collect money for a Gulating memorial and stresses that the outlay for each would not be large if everyone in the old “Gulating law district” took part. In a note under the article the paper adds that “this is an excellent idea.” In “Gula Tidend” for 1 August 1912 Otto has a note reporting what had come in so far. “As you can see, the collection is not going fast”, he writes. In all, including interest, the collection account in Gulen Sparebank then stood at 63.75 kroner. He had expected more support for the cause. From the figures I see that the largest single sum had come from the youth society Gula in Austgulfjorden.
blocks.8: For the period up to the appointment of the working committee in 1917, I have seen no material other than newspaper articles quarrelling about where the right assembly site lay. Many places are mentioned, but at that time the contributions mostly concerned the parsonage and the area at Flolid, and then, as later, there were many champions on both sides.
blocks.9: One of those who perhaps did more than anyone to bring about a Gulating memorial was Anders Skåsheim from Balestrand. He worked at Landsbanken in Bergen, later as deputy manager at Vestlandsbanken, and was very interested in our history, perhaps especially the Gulating and the value the assembly and the law had for our people. He writes later: “Midtun first took up the cause. But he had to lay it down again”. It was surely Skåsheim who was behind it when the historical society for Sogn took the initiative to appoint a working committee in 1917. The committee was made up as follows:
blocks.10: G.F. Heiberg, chairman, A. Skåsheim, vice-chairman, from the historical society, and from Gulen municipality Otto J. Midtun and Karl L. Birknes were elected, with I. Svardal as deputy. Otto Midtun became treasurer and Birknes “assistant”. Karl L. Birknes is the well-known local historian whom everyone in Gulen, and many more, knows as Karl Gåta, and he surely became an excellent assistant. Skåsheim became secretary of the committee. When Otto J. Midtun died in 1923, the mayor Hans K. Rutledal was elected as Gulen municipality's representative.
blocks.11: The committee drew on many “knowledgeable men”. Names I see from the minute book as having been involved are: Professor Haakon Shetelig, the head teacher E.C. Bendixen, Dr Just Bing, Professor Gjelsvik, Professor Koht, the farmer Hans Flolid, the teacher Jacob Aaland, the newspaper editor Albert Joleik, Professor Magnus Olsen and the state veterinarian S. Tillier.
blocks.12: In addition they received input from a lively debate in the press, with masses of contributions from both laymen and scholars. Two of the most active writers were Hans Flolid and O. Austgulen. The committee had many meetings and several on-site investigations together with “knowledgeable men”, among them those mentioned above and others.
blocks.13: On 18 August 1918 the committee, with several of its helpers, made a “journey” in Gulen. They visited Eide, Guløy, Flolid and the parsonage. The journey ended with a meeting at which they recommended that the memorial be raised in Eivindvik.
blocks.14: At a meeting on 8 March 1919 they adopted a draft circular “for subscription of gifts for the memorial stone to the Gulating”.
blocks.15: At a meeting on 15 January 1923 the committee found it “useful” for the municipal council “to give its opinion again” after letters had come in opposing the committee's recommendation. “The answer is to be presented at a later meeting of the committee”. No such meeting appears in the minutes. The meeting of 15 January 1923 was this committee's last. From what I have found, a new committee did not start work until 1961.
blocks.16: Despite several statements that the most important thing was to get a memorial even if it might not stand on the exact spot, it seems that it was precisely the debate about “the right assembly site” that was the reason the memorial did not come. Some, both laymen and experts, said that no decision on the location should be made before the site had been established, since it could disrupt the research. Some believed that if the site was Eivindvik, no modern memorial was needed; there we had the old stone crosses. Others claimed that a memorial at the Gulating site must come as a memorial for the whole nation and be of interest beyond the country's borders too. An article in “Gula Tidend” for 24 June 1938 says: “It concerns one of the most noble memorial sites from ancient times in the Germanic countries.”
blocks.17: The debate in the press gradually died down, and things grew quieter around the matter. In the paper “Sogningen” on 25 October 1932 there was a large piece about the Gulating site. It says, among other things, that “The historical society once took the initiative to raise such a memorial out there, but gave up, since people in the district strongly disagreed about where the assembly site had been.” But the idea and the hope of a Gulating memorial were alive. In the Christmas issue of “Gula Tidend” in 1937 the idea of a memorial gathering for the old Gulating was raised, and a grand gathering was held in the parsonage grove on 10 July 1938. There was a great deal of good, fine historical programme. As the reports show, the gathering was a great success. About 4,000 people took part, probably the largest crowd ever gathered in Gulen. The event was a great boost and gave new courage to those working to raise the Gulating memorial. It was also a great encouragement that King Haakon VII visited the village in 1936, when Professor Olav Midttun spoke so warmly on Lovseiingsberget about the village's link with history and the Gulating that the king had to take out his handkerchief and dry his eyes.
blocks.18: From the years that followed I have found little about the work on raising the memorial, but Anders Skåsheim did not give up; he kept track of things and looked after the material collected. The dispute over the choice of site died down. Skåsheim, who was the only surviving member of the committee elected in 1917, contacted the mayor Kjellevold in 1960 about appointing a new committee. After a meeting of Gulen municipal council, a “gathering meeting” concerning the Gulating site was held on 15 October 1960, attended by council members and other interested people. At the invitation of the history society and the executive committee, A. Skåsheim gave a talk on the subject. A discussion followed. Among those present was O. Austgulen, who had earlier been heavily involved in the matter with many newspaper articles. It was decided to appoint a new committee. This was done in 1961, with the county governor N. Schei, the mayor Kjellevold and the head of schools S. Randal as members.
blocks.19: In 1966 Nord- og Midthordland Sogelag had its 50th anniversary and held its “summer outing” at Flolid. On 3 July they held a gathering there and commemorated the Gulating with a historical programme.
blocks.20: The material Skåsheim had kept from earlier work was handed over to the new committee when it started work. From various quarters there were wishes for more research, and the committee had several investigations carried out by experts. Both now and earlier, comparisons were made with other old assembly sites. The Norwegian Arts Council was involved. Archaeological and botanical investigations were carried out both at the parsonage and at Flolid, by the scientific assistant Ingvild Øye Sølvberg and by Professor Knut Helle.
blocks.21: A later committee also included Professor Hagen and the curator Per Fett.
blocks.22: In 1974 Schei wrote to the mayor of Gulen that, as the only surviving member of the 1961 committee, he wished to report on what the committee had done and to complete its work. This took place at a meeting with the executive committee at Brekkestranda guesthouse on 21 October 1974. In addition to an oral report, a written account was submitted. At the meeting it was agreed to appoint a new committee.
blocks.23: On 10 May 1982 a meeting was held in Eivindvik with the aim “of getting a cultural programme – and later more – going in connection with the Gulating site.” The mayor Olav Solheim had arranged the meeting. Present were: the county culture director Lidvin Osland, the county curator Gunhild Systad, the head of schools Bjarne Dåe, the bank manager Magnor Midtun and the vice-chair of Gulen culture board, Thorbjørg Birknes, who wrote the minutes of the meeting. “Magnor Midtun gave a short overview of what we know about the Gulating”. “We do not know for certain where the assembly was held, and we quickly concluded that in this connection it matters less. We know that the Gulating was held in Gulen, and for us it is important to find a suitable venue where the programme can be performed.” Various forms of possible programme were discussed, and site visits were made at Flolid and in Eivindvik.
blocks.24: When the idea of a Gulating memorial was first raised early in the 20th century, the intention was to raise a stone monument. It was such a memorial that the 1917 committee proposed to put up in front of the church.
blocks.25: People felt it was slow going to get a memorial put up. There were driving forces in the village who pushed on; the matter became a topic of conversation among the people, and gradually the idea of a historical play became what people were most concerned with. But the wheels still turned slowly, and so many historical plays appeared around the country that one could almost speak of inflation in such plays. Gradually the idea of a multi-purpose venue came up. To put more life into the matter, it was proposed to bring the well-known clairvoyant Anna Elisabeth Westerlund here. She was here from 6 to 11 April 1983 and “pointed out the site of the Gulating”, as a newspaper report put it. This led to much publicity and a great deal of discussion and media attention about the Gulating, both locally and in the rest of the country. Many newspapers and NRK came here, and the magazine “Allers” had a large article with pictures from Westerlund's visit. Whether this had any effect on progress I cannot say, but later in the 1980s the work gathered pace.
blocks.26: On 7 October 1985 a new meeting was held in Eivindvik with the following participants: Anne Gullestad, Hans Jacob Sandanger, Erling Øvstedal, Bjarne Dåe, Magnor Midtun and Ola Byrknes. Mayor Byrknes had arranged the meeting after several conversations with the county culture director Osland. In the note the mayor made of the meeting we see, among other things, that “It was further stressed that the municipality regards financial and professional involvement from the county authority and central government as decisive for carrying out such a project.” This time too the participants made a site visit “in the Eivindvik/Flolid area” and concluded that also as regards the choice of venue “experts must be brought in.” At a meeting on 21 February 1986 the municipal culture board agreed that Flolid was best suited “for this purpose.”
blocks.27: Mayor Ola Byrknes showed great interest in the matter. He was one of those who surely saw more clearly than most that the Gulating memorial was a very important cause, of great value not only for our municipality but for the whole nation. According to the case material I have seen, he stressed this on many occasions, both in meetings with cultural figures and authorities and otherwise.
blocks.28: In the period that followed, several reports were written and many meetings held both locally and at county level. The matter now gained a broader base as more and more people and organisations were brought in: people with historical knowledge, other cultural figures, people from the church, legal experts, the county's cultural department and the county authorities. On 4 December 1989 a meeting was held at Sunnfjord Hotel, chaired by the county culture director, with participants from the diocese, the county governor, the county culture director, Sogn og Fjordane theatre, Gulen municipality and its cultural department, the history professor Knut Helle and the professor of legal history Gudmund Sandvik. Here it was agreed to set up a main committee called the Gulating Council and a smaller working group of 3–5 members. The Gulating Council was broadly composed of representatives of the bodies mentioned above and Professor Knut Helle. The working group consisted of the county governor, the county culture director and the mayor of Gulen. Later a reference group was also set up. On the 19th of the same month Gulen municipal council decided to create a full-time post, “initially as a two-year engagement, with the Gulating as its primary task.”
blocks.29: When it was made clear that Flolid was to be the main arena, with the area by the church, the stone crosses, St Olav's spring etc. as part of a whole, the municipal council, despite strong voices against taking on such large costs, decided to enter into negotiations with the landowners at Flolid to secure land for the memorial project. After negotiations, valuation and a higher valuation, the municipal council accepted the higher valuation in case 135/96.
blocks.30: Ideas for commemorations were invited and many proposals came in. Four bids came in for a pre-project for the main arena, and at a meeting on 7 August 1990 the working group, after consulting the reference group, gave the commission to the landscape architects Kalve & Støle A/S and Arkitektkontoret 4B, represented by Valborg Leivestad, working together. The architects presented the draft project, and it was discussed at a meeting at the county culture director's office on 10 January 1991, attended by the working group and the reference group among others. The draft was presented at a public meeting at Eivindvik school on 24 August 1991. Many spoke there, and many proposals came in here too. The plans were also put out for inspection and comment in several places in the municipality.
blocks.31: There was agreement that the Gulating site must become a resource for experiences where one can both learn about history and relax. Names for the project were discussed, and since 1985 the site at Flolid has been called “Gulatingsparken” (the Gulating Park).
blocks.32: Håkonarspelet at the Millennium Site at Flolid before the development – the finale during the royal visit in 2002. Photo: Unknown.
blocks.33: In the mid-1990s “Håkonarspelet” (the Håkon play) came into the picture as a first commemoration in the Gulating Park and of the Gulating memorial. It is written about elsewhere, but I will mention here that it was part of the “Coastal History Weeks”, led by Ragnhild Randal, and became a huge voluntary effort involving people from the whole municipality.
blocks.34: Ragnhild Randal and Anne Gullestad were the driving forces, but they had many committed local helpers. Gullestad was the director. A temporary stage was built from scratch, and masses of costumes and props were sewn and built. Apart from a few professional actors, all the performers were from the municipality, and after about half a year of rehearsals the first performances were on 23 and 24 August 1997. The play was a great success that spurred further joint effort. In 2001 Professor Knut Helle's book “Gulatinget og Gulatingslova” (The Gulating and the Gulating law) was published. An excellent work that presented in a good and accessible way what the assembly and the law stood for. Knowledge of our forefathers is good ballast to carry with us. I have read that a people with no past has no future either. The book, and the fact that Helle himself came here to introduce it and wrote dedications for those who wished, also helped to promote interest in the Gulating. And the interest grew greater and greater and more and more positive as concrete things happened in the work of commemorating the assembly.
blocks.35: At a meeting on 7 December 1999 the county council of Sogn og Fjordane decided that the Gulating should be the millennium site for our county. A main committee was elected with the following members: Bishop Ole D. Hagesæther, the county director Lidvin Osland, the county mayor Knut Aarethun, Professor Knut Helle, the district judge Bjarte Eikeset and, from Gulen, the mayor Ola E. Byrknes and the head of culture and business Harald Haugejorden. This was a joyful event for us here; now we reckoned that the project was secured both financially and professionally. Through cooperation between the municipality and the county, things moved forward quickly. The sculptor Bård Breivik was engaged and Martine Rød was appointed project manager.
blocks.36: The first Gulating seminar was held on 1–2 September 2000, with an “expert seminar” on Friday 1 September in the council chamber and a “public seminar” on Saturday 2 September in the community hall “Vårtun”. After the “public seminar” Eivindvik youth society opened an “assembly café” with “food and cultural entertainment”, and at 6 p.m. the county's millennium trees were planted at Flolid by the chair of the culture committee of Sogn og Fjordane, the mayor of Gulen and the municipality's newly elected youth council. The millennium trees, “12 columnar junipers”, were supplied by Åberge nursery in Sogndal.
blocks.37: The unveiling of “Seidmann”, Bård Breivik's first sculpture for “the Gulating Millennium Site”, was performed on 8 November 2001 by the state secretary Berit Gjerløw Øksnes. This took place in connection with the launch of Professor Helle's book “Gulatinget og Gulatingslova”.
blocks.38: A decision by the county administration on 9 April 2002 says: “Sogn og Fjordane county takes responsibility for the further work on the millennium site ‘the Gulating’, and takes over as project owner”.
blocks.39: In 2002 the people of Gulen had yet another pleasant experience: King Harald and Queen Sonja visited the municipality. It was especially fine for the roughly 100 performers who showed “Håkonarspelet” to the royal couple. In miserable rain they gave a fine performance and received great applause and much well-deserved praise. In a television interview the king said roughly this: “We got to experience Western Norway at its wettest, but the play was so interesting that we did not notice the rain.”
blocks.40: Now we rejoice that the work of designing and completing the Gulating memorial is so well under way after 100 years of strife and toil. We trust that our politicians, those carrying out the work and others involved in this responsible task will make the Gulating Park a worthy memorial where everyone can wander about in a beautiful and inspiring setting, and, together with measures in the area by the church and the old stone crosses, create a true people's memorial where one feels the breath of history flow and enters into the role Gulen has played in our history.
blocks.41: What is written here is based on information from old newspaper articles, the minute book of the 1917 working committee and transcripts of the work in Gulen municipality. Thanks to everyone who has helped me! Special thanks to Hermod Kleppa at the county archives in Sogn og Fjordane, who has done a tremendous job of bringing out so much old material!
blocks.42: M. Midtun reads a prologue at the seminar on the opening day. Photo: Unknown.
blocks.43: "This article was written early in 2003, and on 27 August 2005 the Gulating Millennium Site was opened at Flolid. There was broad coverage in the media – newspapers, radio and television. Much has been written in praise of this opening ceremony, but I would still like to mention here that it was a most memorable occasion with many well-known people present. Prime Minister Kjell Magne Bondevik was among the speakers at the Gulating seminar in the morning. Through the day there were various programmes and activities; among other things, extracts were shown from Håkonarspelet and from the international show by students at United World College in Flekke. The project manager Martine Rød, the mayor Trude Brosvik and the county mayor Nils R. Sandal all had a busy and exciting day. The opening itself was performed by the President of the Storting, Jørgen Kosmo. He brought a copy of a medieval bell as a gift from the Storting to the Gulating Millennium Site. Olemic Thommessen's piece "Mot Gulating" (Towards the Gulating) was performed at Tinghella. With Svein Tindberg in the lead role, Jens Uwe Korten's projection of pictures and film on the Tingveggen (assembly wall), and Palle Mikkelborg's music, performed by Førde Chamber Choir and others, it was a performance we will long remember.
blocks.44: In all, close to 2,000 people turned up, and even though the weather was not of the best, it was a splendid opening of the millennium site.
blocks.45: The next day, Sunday, the celebration continued with a festive service led by the Bishop of Bjørgvin, Ole D. Hagesæther, assisted by Dean Geir Sørebø, the parish priest Jens Linde and several other priests from the diocese. The gift from the Storting was then used as a “church bell”. The service included much fine singing and music. The weather was fine, and many people turned up then too. It was a very fine gathering, and the whole weekend became a great festival for the people.
blocks.46: As the first item, before the items on the set programme of the celebration, at the seminar on Saturday morning, I gave a prologue, and I include an extract from it here:
blocks.47: PROLOGUE FOR THE OPENING OF THE MILLENNIUM SITE
blocks.48: The Millennium Site is approved as a place for weddings in the diocese of Bjørgvin, and on the Saturday after the opening the first bridal couple were married here. They wished to hear the prologue from the opening again, and it was read with the following addition:
blocks.49: The first bridal couple married at our Millennium Site
blocks.50: today stand happily in the park as rightful husband and wife;
blocks.52: have here locked themselves into marriage.
blocks.53: We want to greet you warmly
blocks.54: and wish you the best of luck!
blocks.55: The first bridal couple married at the Gulating Millennium Site arrived by horse and carriage. Photo: Unknown.
